newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia bought U.S. maize in late '96 - grains source.
newsitem.headline: Russia bought U.S. maize in late '96 - grains source.

text.p: A senior Russian grains source said on Wednesday that one or several Russian organisations bought several 12,000-tonne cargoes of U.S. No. 2 corn (maize) at the end of last year.
The imports, delivered in November and December 1996 via the Latvian port of Riga, have not yet shown up in Russia's State Customs Committee figures, which track most deliveries.
The source said the imported maize was sold on the domestic market for around $187 per tonne.

Agriculture Minister Viktor Khklystun said in September 1996 that Russia would import 4.0-4.5 million tonnes of maize and soymeal to supplement the 1996 harvest, with maize purchases three times higher than soymeal purchases.
But one grains trader has estimated Russia's total maize imports over the 1996/1997 crop marketing year will reach only 120,000 tonnes as livestock numbers fall.
Russia's maize crop last year fell 38 percent year-on-year to a gross 1.5 million tonnes, a farm analyst said.
Russia's official 1996 net grain harvest was 69.0 million tonnes, the second lowest in three decades and the second poor harvest in a row.
